title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 54 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 407–410 (Night 54, continuing directly from nights-53), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 54 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The bath-stoker nurses the sick Ḍawʾ al-Makān back to health with sugar, rose-water and boiled chickens, takes him to the bath, and at last hears his story; Ḍawʾ al-Makān weeps for his sister and asks to be sent to Damascus, and the stoker and his wife decide to travel with him. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ وَالْخَمْسُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-rābiʿatu wa-al-khamsūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fourth and the fiftieth.
sentences.i: And when it was the fifty-fourth night,
sentences.n: The night formula again; the ordinal is compound ('the fourth and the fiftieth') and stands in the nominative.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْوَقَّادَ قَالَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-waqqāda qāla
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O happy king, that the stoker said:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O happy king, that the stoker said:
sentences.n: al-Waqqād is the furnace-man of the bath who took in the sick boy Ḍawʾ al-Makān.

sentences.t: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ بِسِرِّكَ الْمَكْنُونِ أَنْ تَجْعَلَ حَيْوَةَ هَذَا الصَّبِيِّ عَلَى يَدَيَّ
sentences.tr: allāhumma innī asʾaluka bi-sirrika al-maknūni an tajʿala ḥaywata hādhā al-ṣabiyyi ʿalā yadayya
sentences.l: O God, truly-I I-ask-you by your secret, the hidden, that you make the life of this boy upon my hands.
sentences.i: O God, I ask you by your hidden secret to let this boy's life be restored at my hands.
sentences.n: The edition spells 'life' حيوة (ḥayāh), with a waw, an older orthography; we keep it. 'Upon my hands' means 'through my agency'.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَ الْوَقَّادُ يَتَعَهَّدُهُ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَهُوَيَسْقِيهِ السُّكَّرَ وَمَاءَ الْخِلَافِ وَمَاءَ الْوَرْدِ وَيَتَعَطَّفُ عَلَيْهِ وَيَتَلَطَّفُ بِهِ حَتَّى سَرَتِ الصِّحَّةُ فِي جِسْمِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla al-waqqādu yataʿahhaduhu thalāthata ayyāmin wa-huwayasqīhi al-sukkara wa-māʾa al-khilāfi wa-māʾa al-wardi wa-yataʿaṭṭafu ʿalayhi wa-yatalaṭṭafu bihi ḥattā sarati al-ṣiḥḥatu fī jismihi
sentences.l: And the stoker did not cease tending-him three days, and he-was-giving-him-to-drink the sugar and the water of the willow and the water of the rose, and showing-tenderness to him and being-gentle with him, until the health crept into his body.
sentences.i: The stoker kept on nursing him for three days, giving him sugar-water, willow-water and rose-water to drink, treating him with tenderness and gentleness, until health crept back into his body.
sentences.n: The edition prints وهويسقيه ('and he was giving him to drink') as one word, and we keep it so. ثلثة is the printed short spelling of ثلاثة, 'three'. Willow-water (māʾ al-khilāf) was a cooling restorative.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ عَيْنَيْهِ فَدَخَلَ الْوَقَّادُ عَلَيْهِ فَرَآهُ جَالِسًا وَعَلَيْهِ آثَارُ النَّشٰطِ
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥa ḍawʾu al-makāni ʿaynayhi fa-dakhala al-waqqādu ʿalayhi fa-raʾāhu jālisan wa-ʿalayhi āthāru al-nashāṭi
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān opened his two eyes, and the stoker entered upon him and saw-him sitting, and upon him the traces of the liveliness.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān opened his eyes, and when the stoker came in he found him sitting up, with the marks of returning vigour on him.
sentences.n: Ḍawʾ al-Makān means 'Light of the Place' and is the boy's name. النشط is printed short for النشاط, 'liveliness'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ مَا حَالُكَ يَا وَلَدِي فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu mā ḥāluka yā waladī fī hādhā al-waqti
sentences.l: And he said to him: What is your state, O my son, at this time?
sentences.i: He said to him: How are you, my son, at this hour?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَمْدُ اللَّهِ فَإِنِّي بِخَيْرٍ وَعَافِيَةٍ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥamdu allāhi fa-innī bi-khayrin wa-ʿāfiyatin in shāʾa allāhu taʿālā fī hādhā al-waqti
sentences.l: And he said: The praise, God; for I am in good and well-being, if God the Exalted wills, at this time.
sentences.i: He said: Praise be to God, for I am well and healthy at this hour, God Most High willing.
sentences.n: The edition prints الحمد الله without the lām of لله; the sense is plainly 'praise be to God', and the next speech in the night has it written out in full.

sentences.t: فَحَمِدَ الْوَقَّادُ الْمَوْلَى عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَنَهَضَ إِلَى السُّوقِ وَاشْتَرَى لَهُ عَشَرَةَ فَرَارِيجَ وَأَتَى بِهِمْ إِلَى زَوْجَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥamida al-waqqādu al-mawlā ʿalā dhālika wa-nahaḍa ilā al-sūqi wa-ishtarā lahu ʿasharata farārīja wa-atā bihim ilā zawjatihi
sentences.l: And the stoker praised the Master for that, and rose to the market, and bought for him ten chickens, and came with them to his wife.
sentences.i: The stoker thanked the Lord for that, went to the market, bought ten chickens for the boy, and brought them to his wife.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا اِذْ بَحِي لَهُ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ اثْنَيْنِ بَاكِرَ النَّهَارِ وَاحِدًا وَآخِرَ النَّهَارِ وَاحِدًا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā idh baḥī lahu fī kulli yawmin ithnayni bākira al-nahāri wāḥidan wa-ākhira al-nahāri wāḥidan
sentences.l: And he said to her: Slaughter for him, in every day, two: at the early-part of the day one, and at the last-part of the day one.
sentences.i: He told her: Kill two chickens for him each day, one early in the day and one at the end of it.
sentences.n: The edition prints the imperative اذبحي split in two, اذ بحي, and we keep the split; read it as one word, idhbaḥī, 'slaughter!'.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتْ وَذَبَحَتْ لَهُ فَرُّوجًا وَسَلَقَتْهُ وَأَتَتْ بِهِ إِلَيْهِ وَأَطْعَمَتْهُ إِيَّاهُ وَأَسْقَتْهُ مَرَقَتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmat wa-dhabaḥat lahu farrūjan wa-salaqathu wa-atat bihi ilayhi wa-aṭʿamathu iyyāhu wa-asqathu maraqatahu
sentences.l: And she rose and slaughtered for him a chicken, and boiled it, and came with it to him, and fed-him it, and gave-him-to-drink its broth.
sentences.i: She got up, killed a chicken for him, boiled it, brought it to him, fed it to him and gave him its broth to drink.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنَ الْأَكْلِ قَدَّمَتْ لَهُ مَاوْ حَارًّا فَغَسَلَ يَدَيْهِ وَاتَّكَأً عَلَى الْوِسَادَةِ وَغَطَّتْهُ بِمِلَاءَةٍ فَنَامَ إِلَى الْعَصْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha mina al-akli qaddamat lahu māw ḥārran fa-ghasala yadayhi wa-ittakaʾa ʿalā al-wisādati wa-ghaṭṭathu bi-milāʾatin fa-nāma ilā al-ʿaṣri
sentences.l: And when he finished from the eating, she presented to him water hot, and he washed his two hands and reclined upon the cushion, and she covered-him with a wrap, and he slept until the afternoon.
sentences.i: When he had finished eating, she brought him hot water; he washed his hands and leaned back on the cushion, and she covered him with a sheet, and he slept until the afternoon.
sentences.n: ماو is the edition's spelling here for ماء, 'water'; we read it as māʾ and vocalise it as printed. The mark on واتكاً is the edition's own; the verb is ittakaʾa, 'reclined'.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتْ وَسَلَقَتْ لَهُ فَرُّوجًا آخَرَ وَأَتَتْ بِهِ لَهُ وَفَسَخَتْهُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ كُلْ يَا وَلَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāmat wa-salaqat lahu farrūjan ākhara wa-atat bihi lahu wa-fasakhathu wa-qālat lahu kul yā waladī
sentences.l: And she rose and boiled for him another chicken, and came with it to him, and pulled-it-apart, and said to him: Eat, O my son.
sentences.i: She got up and boiled another chicken for him, brought it to him, pulled it apart, and said to him: Eat, my son.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ يَأْكُلُ وَإِذَا بِزَوْجِهَا قَدْ دَخَلَ فَوَجَدَهَا تُطْعِمُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa yaʾkulu wa-idhā bi-zawjihā qad dakhala fa-wajadahā tuṭʿimuhu
sentences.l: And while he was eating, and behold, with her husband, he had entered, and he found her feeding him.
sentences.i: While he was eating, her husband came in and found her feeding him.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِـ ('and behold') marks a sudden arrival; the bi- here only introduces what appears.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ جَلَسَ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ مَا حَالُكَ يَا وَلَدِي الْآنَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu jalasa ʿinda raʾsihi wa-qāla lahu mā ḥāluka yā waladī al-āna
sentences.l: Then, truly-he, he sat by his head and said to him: What is your state, O my son, now?
sentences.i: Then he sat down by the boy's head and said: How are you now, my son?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى الْعَافِيَةِ جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ عَنِّي خَيْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥamdu li-allāhi ʿalā al-ʿāfiyati jazāka allāhu ʿannī khayran
sentences.l: And he said: The praise to God for the well-being; may God requite you from me with good.
sentences.i: He said: Praise be to God for my health. May God reward you well on my behalf.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْوَقَّادُ بِذَلِكَ ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ خَرَجَ وَأَتَى لَهُ بِشَرَابِ الْبَنَفْسَجِ وَمَاءِ الْوَرْدِ وَسَقَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-waqqādu bi-dhālika thumma innahu kharaja wa-atā lahu bi-sharābi al-banafsaji wa-māʾi al-wardi wa-saqāhu
sentences.l: And the stoker rejoiced at that; then, truly-he, he went out and came to him with the syrup of the violet and the water of the rose, and gave-him-to-drink.
sentences.i: The stoker was glad at that. Then he went out and came back with violet syrup and rose-water and gave it to him to drink.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ الْوَقَّادُ يَعْمَلُ فِى الْحَمَّامِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ بِخَمْسَةِ دَرَاهِمَ فَيَشْتَرِي لَهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ بِدِرْهَمٍ سُكَّرًا وَمَاءَ الْوَرْدِ وَشَرَابَ الْبَنَفْسَجِ وَمَاءَ الْخِلَافِ وَيَشْتَرِي لَهُ بِدِرْهَمٍ فَرَارِيجَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna dhālika al-waqqādu yaʿmalu fī al-ḥammāmi kulla yawmin bi-khamsati darāhima fa-yashtarī lahu kulla yawmin bi-dirhamin sukkaran wa-māʾa al-wardi wa-sharāba al-banafsaji wa-māʾa al-khilāfi wa-yashtarī lahu bi-dirhamin farārīja
sentences.l: And that stoker was working in the bath every day for five dirhams, and he would buy for him every day for a dirham sugar and the water of the rose and the syrup of the violet and the water of the willow, and buy for him for a dirham chickens.
sentences.i: Now this stoker worked in the bath for five dirhams a day, and every day he spent one dirham on sugar, rose-water, violet syrup and willow-water for the boy, and another dirham on chickens.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَ يُلَاطِفُهُ إِلَى أَنْ مَضَى عَلَيْهِ شَهْرٌ مِنَ الزَّمَانِ حَتَّى زَالَتْ عَنْهُ آثَارُ الْمَرَضِ وَقَدْ تَوَجَّهَتْ لَهُ الْعَافِيَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla yulāṭifuhu ilā an maḍā ʿalayhi shahrun mina al-zamāni ḥattā zālat ʿanhu āthāru al-maraḍi wa-qad tawajjahat lahu al-ʿāfiyatu
sentences.l: And he did not cease being-kind-to-him until a month of the time passed over him, until the traces of the sickness departed from him, and well-being had turned toward him.
sentences.i: He kept on caring for him until a month had passed, by which time every trace of the illness had left him and health had turned his way.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْوَقَّادُ وَزَوْجَتُهُ بِعَافِيَةِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-waqqādu wa-zawjatuhu bi-ʿāfiyati ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: And the stoker and his wife rejoiced at the well-being of Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.i: The stoker and his wife rejoiced at Ḍawʾ al-Makān's recovery.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ يَا وَلَدِي هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ مَعِي الْحَمَّامَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu yā waladī hal laka an tadkhula maʿī al-ḥammāma
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: O my son, is there for you that you enter with me the bath?
sentences.i: The stoker said to him: My son, would you like to come into the bath with me?
sentences.n: هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ … ('is there for you that …') is the usual way of offering something: 'would you like to …?'

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam
sentences.l: He said: Yes.
sentences.i: He said, "Yes."

sentences.t: فَمَضَى إِلَى السُّوقِ وَأَتَى لَهُ بِمُكَارِى وَأَرْكَبَهُ عَلَى حِمَارٍ وَجَعَلَ يُسْنِدُهُ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ مَعَهُ إِلَى الْحَمَّامِ فَأَجْلَسَهُ وَأَدْخَلَ الْحِمَارَ إِلَى الْمُسْتَوْقَدِ
sentences.tr: fa-maḍā ilā al-sūqi wa-atā lahu bi-mukārī wa-arkabahu ʿalā ḥimārin wa-jaʿala yusniduhu ilā an waṣala maʿahu ilā al-ḥammāmi fa-ajlasahu wa-adkhala al-ḥimāra ilā al-mustawqadi
sentences.l: And he went to the market and brought for him, with a muleteer, and mounted him upon a donkey, and began supporting him until he arrived with him at the bath; and seated him, and made the donkey enter into the stoking-room.
sentences.i: So he went off to the market and came back with a muleteer, set Ḍawʾ al-Makān on a donkey, and kept him propped upright until they reached the bathhouse. There he sat him down and led the donkey into the furnace room.
sentences.n: The sentence does not name Ḍawʾ al-Makān, but he is the one mounted and propped up, and the stoker (al-waqqād) is the subject throughout. مُكَارِى is the muleteer, printed with final ى; we keep the printed spelling. الْمُسْتَوْقَدُ is the place where the fire is kept, the bath's furnace room, where the stoker works.

sentences.t: وَمَضَى إِلَى السُّوقِ وَاشْتَرَى لَهُ سِدْرًا وَدُقَاقًا وَقَالَ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ يَاسَيِّدِي بِسْمِ اللَّهِ اُدْخُلْ اِغْسِلْ لَكَ جَسَدَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-maḍā ilā al-sūqi wa-ishtarā lahu sidran wa-duqāqan wa-qāla li-Ḍawʾi al-makāni yāsayyidī bi-smi Allāhi udkhul ighsil laka jasadaka
sentences.l: And he went to the market and bought for him lote-leaf and fine-powder, and said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān: O my master, in the name of God, enter, wash for yourself your body.
sentences.i: Then he went back to the market and bought sidr leaf and fine soap-powder for him, and said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān, "My lord, in God's name, go in and wash your body."
sentences.n: سِدْر (lote-tree leaf, ground for washing) and دُقَاق (fine powder, here a cleansing powder) are the bath-supplies. The edition prints يا سيدي as one word, يَاسَيِّدِي, and we keep it. اُدْخُلْ اِغْسِلْ are two imperatives set side by side without a conjunction, 'go in, wash'. لَكَ is the 'dative of interest': 'wash for yourself'.

sentences.t: نَدْخُلُ هُوَ وَإِيَّاهُ إِلَى دَاخِلِ الْحَمَّامِ وَأَخَذَ الْوَقَّادُ يَحُكُّ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ رِجْلَيْهِ وَشَرَعَ يَغْسِلُ لَهُ جَسَدَهُ بِالسِّدْرِ وَالدُّقَاقِ
sentences.tr: nadkhulu huwa wa-iyyāhu ilā dākhili al-ḥammāmi wa-akhadha al-waqqādu yaḥukku li-Ḍawʾi al-makāni rijlayhi wa-sharaʿa yaghsilu lahu jasadahu bi-al-sidri wa-al-duqāqi
sentences.l: We-enter, he and he-himself, to the inside of the bath; and the stoker took to scrubbing for Ḍawʾ al-Makān his two feet, and began washing for him his body with the lote-leaf and the fine-powder.
sentences.i: They went into the inner bath together, and the stoker began to scrub Ḍawʾ al-Makān's feet and then to wash his whole body with the sidr and the powder.
sentences.n: نَدْخُلُ is printed as a first-person plural ('we enter'). The sense wants a past narrative verb, 'they entered' (perhaps a misprint for دخلا), so we vocalise what is printed and translate by the sense. هُوَ وَإِيَّاهُ, literally 'he and him', means 'the two of them together'. أَخَذَ and شَرَعَ followed by a present verb mean 'began to'.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِبَلَّانٍ قَدْ أَرْسَلَهُ مُعَلِّمُ الْحَمَّامِ إِلَى ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ فَوَجَدَ الْوَقَّادَ يَغْسِلُهُ وَيَحُكُّ رِجْلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-ballānin qad arsalahu muʿallimu al-ḥammāmi ilā Ḍawʾi al-makāni fa-wajada al-waqqāda yaghsiluhu wa-yaḥukku rijlayhi
sentences.l: And behold, with a bath-attendant whom the master of the bath had sent to Ḍawʾ al-Makān; and he found the stoker washing him and scrubbing his two feet.
sentences.i: Then, behold, an attendant whom the bathhouse master had sent to look after Ḍawʾ al-Makān arrived, and he found the stoker washing him and scrubbing his feet.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِـ … 'and behold …': the بِـ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what suddenly appears. The بَلَّان is the bath-attendant who shaves and washes clients; the مُعَلِّم is the master or owner of the bath.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ إِلَيْهِ الْبَلَّانُ وَقَالَ لَهُ هَذَا نَقْصٌ فِي حَقِّ الْمُعَلِّمِ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama ilayhi al-ballānu wa-qāla lahu hādhā naqṣun fī ḥaqqi al-muʿallimi
sentences.l: So the bath-attendant advanced to him and said to him: This is a deficiency in the right of the master.
sentences.i: The attendant came up to him and said, "This is a slight against the master's honour."
sentences.n: 'A deficiency in the right of the master' means that it reflects badly on the master that a guest should be washed by someone else.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَقَّادُ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ غَمَرَنَا بِإِحْسَانِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-waqqādu wa-Allāhi inna al-muʿallima ghamaranā bi-iḥsānihi
sentences.l: And the stoker said: By God, indeed the master has flooded us with his beneficence.
sentences.i: The stoker replied, "By God, the master has overwhelmed us with his kindness."

sentences.t: فَشَرَعَ الْبَلَّانُ يَحْلِقُ رَأْسَ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ ثُمَّ اغْتَسَلَ هُوَ وَالْوَقَّادُ
sentences.tr: fa-sharaʿa al-ballānu yaḥliqu raʾsa Ḍawʾi al-makāni thumma ightasala huwa wa-al-waqqādu
sentences.l: So the bath-attendant began to shave the head of Ḍawʾ al-Makān; then he washed himself, he and the stoker.
sentences.i: So the attendant set about shaving Ḍawʾ al-Makān's head, and afterwards Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the stoker bathed themselves.
sentences.n: The printed رَأْس carries a hamza the edition itself prints. In ثُمَّ اغْتَسَلَ هُوَ وَالْوَقَّادُ the subject is probably Ḍawʾ al-Makān, 'he', with the stoker joined to him; the Arabic does not say who 'he' is.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَتَى بِهِ الْوَقَّادُ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ وَأَلْبَسَهُ قَمِيصًا رَفِيعًا وَثَوْبًا مِنْ ثِيَابِهِ وَعِمَامَةً لَطِيفَةً وَحِزَامًا رَفِيعًا وَلَفَّ لَهُ شَدَّ عَلَى رَقَبَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika atā bihi al-waqqādu ilā manzilihi wa-albasahu qamīṣan rafīʿan wa-thawban min thiyābihi wa-ʿimāmatan laṭīfatan wa-ḥizāman rafīʿan wa-laffa lahu shadda ʿalā raqabatihi
sentences.l: And after that the stoker brought him to his house, and clothed him with a fine shirt, and a garment from his garments, and a delicate turban, and a fine belt, and wound for him a binding upon his neck.
sentences.i: After that the stoker brought him home, dressed him in a fine shirt, a robe of his own, a dainty turban and a fine belt, and wound a scarf about his neck.
sentences.n: شَدّ is a wrapping or binding; around the neck it is presumably a scarf or neck-cloth, though the exact garment is not certain. أَتَى بِهِ is 'bring him' (the verb takes بِـ for the thing brought).

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ زَوْجَةُ الْوَقَّادِ ذَبَحَتْ لَهُ فَرُّوجَيْنِ وَطَبَخَهُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-kānat zawjatu al-waqqādi dhabaḥat lahu farrūjayni wa-ṭabakhahumā
sentences.l: And the wife of the stoker had slaughtered for him two chickens and cooked them.
sentences.i: Now the stoker's wife had slaughtered two young chickens for him and cooked them.
sentences.n: وَكَانَتْ … ذَبَحَتْ: kāna with a past verb gives the pluperfect, 'had slaughtered'. The فَرُّوج is a young chicken, a pullet. The edition prints وَطَبَخَهُمَا without the feminine ending (a masculine 'he cooked them'); we vocalise what is printed, though the wife is evidently the cook, so we translate 'cooked them'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا طَلَعَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَجَلَسَ عَلَى الْفِرَاشِ قَامَ الْوَقَّادُ وَإِذَا بِ لَهُ السُّكَّرُ فِي مَاءِ الْخِلَافِ وَسَقَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṭalaʿa Ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-jalasa ʿalā al-firāshi qāma al-waqqādu wa-idhā bi la-hu al-sukkaru fī māʾi al-khilāfi wa-saqāhu
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān came up and sat upon the bedding, the stoker stood, and behold, with [stray bi] for him the sugar in the water of willow, and gave him to drink.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān had come up and sat down on the bedding, the stoker got up and brought him sugar in willow-water, and gave him it to drink.
sentences.n: The edition prints a stray ب as a word of its own in وَإِذَا ب لَهُ, and we keep the split. It looks like the remnant of a lost phrase, perhaps وَإِذَا بِهِ جَاءَ لَهُ 'and behold, he came to him with'; the sense is plainly that the stoker served him a sugared drink. مَاءُ الْخِلَاف is willow-water, a cooling drink flavoured from the willow flower, like rose-water.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَدَّمَ لَهُ السُّفْرَةَ وَصَارَ الْوَقَّادُ يَفْسَخُ لَهُ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْفَرَارِيجِ وَيُطْعِمُهُ وَيَسْقِيهِ مِنَ الْمَسْلُوقَةِ إِلَى أَنِ اكْتَفَى وَغَسَلَ يَدَيْهِ وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى عَلَى الْعَافِيَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma qaddama lahu al-sufrata wa-ṣāra al-waqqādu yafsakhu lahu min tilka al-farārīji wa-yuṭʿimuhu wa-yasqīhi mina al-maslūqati ilā ani iktafā wa-ghasala yadayhi wa-ḥamida Allāha taʿālā ʿalā al-ʿāfiyati
sentences.l: Then he presented to him the dining-cloth, and the stoker came to be tearing apart for him from those chickens, and feeding him, and giving him to drink from the boiled, until he was satisfied and washed his two hands and praised God the Exalted for the well-being.
sentences.i: Then he set the dining-cloth before him, and the stoker carried on pulling apart pieces of those chickens for him, feeding him and giving him to drink of the broth, until he was satisfied. He washed his hands and thanked God the Most High for his recovered health.
sentences.n: السُّفْرَة is the leather or cloth spread on which a meal is laid out. الْمَسْلُوقَة, 'the boiled', is feminine and presumably stands for the boiled (stewed) dish or its broth. الْعَافِيَة is well-being, health.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِلْوَقَّادِ أَنْتَ الَّذِي مَنَّ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيَّ بِكَ وَجَعَلَ سَلَامَتِي عَلَى يَدَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-al-waqqādi anta alladhī manna Allāhu taʿālā ʿalayya bika wa-jaʿala salāmatī ʿalā yadayka
sentences.l: And he said to the stoker: You are the one by whom God the Exalted has bestowed favour upon me, and has made my safety upon your two hands.
sentences.i: And he said to the stoker, "You are the one through whom God the Most High has shown me favour, and He has placed my deliverance in your hands."
sentences.n: مَنَّ عَلَى is 'bestow a favour on', and here the favour comes through the stoker (بِكَ). 'Upon your two hands' means that his safety came about at the stoker's hands.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ دَعْ عَنْكَ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ وَقُلْ لَنَا مَا سَبَبُ مَجِيئِكَ إِلَى هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ فَإِنِّي أَرَى عَلَى وَجْهِكَ آثَارَ النِّعْمَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu daʿ ʿanka hādhā al-kalāma wa-qul lanā mā sababu majīʾika ilā hādhihi al-madīnati wa-min ayna anta fa-innī arā ʿalā wajhika āthāra al-niʿmati
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: Leave from you this talk, and tell us what is the cause of your coming to this city, and from where you are; for I see upon your face the traces of prosperity.
sentences.i: The stoker said to him, "Enough of such talk. Tell us what brought you to this city and where you come from, for I can see the marks of good fortune on your face."
sentences.n: دَعْ عَنْكَ هَذَا 'leave this off from you' is an idiom for 'enough of that, never mind'. مَجِيئِك keeps the ئ the edition prints. The stoker speaks of 'us' because he speaks for his household.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ قُلْ لِي أَنْتَ كَيْفَ وَقَعْتَ بِي حَتَّى أُخْبِرَكَ بِحَدِيثِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Ḍawʾu al-makāni qul lī anta kayfa waqaʿta bī ḥattā ukhbiraka bi-ḥadīthī
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: Tell me, you, how you fell upon me, so that I may inform you of my story.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him, "First tell me how you came upon me, and then I will tell you my own story."
sentences.n: وَقَعَ بِـ is 'to fall in with, come upon' someone. أَخْبَرَ بِـ is 'to inform of', the verb choosing the preposition.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ أَمَّا أَنَا فَإِنِّي لَمَّا تَوَجَّهْتُ إِلَى أَشْغَالِي وَجَدْتُكَ مَرْمِيًّا عَلَى الْقُمَامَةِ قَرِيبَ الصُّبْحِ عَلَى بَابِ الْمُسْتَوْقَدِ وَلَمْ أَعْرِفْ مَنْ رَمَاكَ فَأَخَذْتُكَ عِنْدِي وَهَذِهِ حِكَايَتِى
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu ammā anā fa-innī lammā tawajjahtu ilā ashghālī wajadtuka marmiyyan ʿalā al-qumāmati qarība al-ṣubḥi ʿalā bābi al-mustawqadi wa-lam aʿrif man ramāka fa-akhadhtuka ʿindī wa-hādhihi ḥikāyatī
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: As for me, indeed when I turned toward my occupations I found you thrown upon the rubbish, near the morning, at the door of the stoking-room, and I did not know who had thrown you; so I took you to be with me, and this is my story.
sentences.i: The stoker said, "As for me, when I set out for my work, I found you thrown down on the rubbish heap near dawn, at the door of the furnace room. I did not know who had thrown you there, so I took you in with me. That is my story."
sentences.n: أَمَّا … فَـ 'as for … then' introduces the speaker's own part, and فَإِنِّي repeats the topic. حِكَايَتِى is printed with final ى and kept so. The accusative قَرِيبَ الصُّبْحِ is adverbial, 'near dawn'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ سُبْحَانَ مَنْ يُحْيِي الْعِظَامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ إِنَّكَ يَا أَخِي مَا فَعَلْتَ الْجَمِيلَ إِلَّامَعَ أَهْلِهِ وَسَتَجْنِي ثَمَرَةَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Ḍawʾu al-makāni subḥāna man yuḥyī al-ʿiẓāma wa-hiya ramīmun innaka yā akhī mā faʿalta al-jamīla illāmaʿa ahlihi wa-sa-tajnī thamarata dhālika
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: Glory to Him who gives life to the bones while they are decayed! Indeed you, O my brother, did not do the fair thing except with its people, and you will gather the fruit of that.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, "Glory be to Him who gives life to bones even when they have rotted away! You, my brother, have shown kindness only to one who deserves it, and you will reap the fruit of it."
sentences.n: سُبْحَانَ مَنْ يُحْيِي الْعِظَامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ echoes the Qurʾān (36:78). The edition prints إِلَّا مَعَ as a single word, الامع, and we keep it joined. 'Did the fair thing only with its people' means that his kindness fell on someone worthy.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَالَ لِلْوَقَّادِ وَأَنَا الْآنَ فِي أَيِّ الْبِلَادِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qāla li-al-waqqādi wa-anā al-āna fī ayyi al-bilādi
sentences.l: Then he said to the stoker: And I, now, in which of the lands?
sentences.i: Then he asked the stoker, "And now, in which country am I?"
sentences.n: The edition prints الْآن with its own precomposed madda, kept as printed. 'In which of the lands' is the ordinary way of asking 'in what country'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَنْتَ فِي مَدِينَةِ الْقُدْسِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu anta fī madīnati al-quds
sentences.l: And he said to him: You are in the city of Jerusalem.
sentences.i: "You are in the city of Jerusalem," he said.
sentences.n: al-Quds, 'the Holy', is Jerusalem.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَهُ ذَلِكَ تَذَكَّرَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ غُرْبَتَهُ وَافْتَكَرَ فِرَاقَ أُخْتِهِ وَبَكَى وَبَاحَ بِسِرِّهِ لِلْوَقَّادِ وَحَكَى لَهُ حِكَايَتَهُ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿindahu dhālika tadhakkara Ḍawʾu al-makāni ghurbatahu wa-iftakara firāqa ukhtihi wa-bakā wa-bāḥa bi-sirrihi li-al-waqqādi wa-ḥakā lahu ḥikāyatahu wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And at him that, Ḍawʾ al-Makān remembered his exile, and thought upon the separation from his sister, and wept, and disclosed his secret to the stoker, and told him his story, and recited, saying:
sentences.i: At that, Ḍawʾ al-Makān remembered his exile and thought of being parted from his sister. He wept, confided his secret to the stoker, told him his tale, and recited:
sentences.n: The edition prints فَعِنْدَهُ ذَلِكَ, literally 'at him, that', where the usual phrase is فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ 'at that'; we keep the printed ه. 'Disclosed his secret' uses بَاحَ بِـ, a verb that takes بِـ for what is divulged. The next lines are verse.

sentences.t:
هُمْ حَمَّلُونِي فِي الْهَوَى غَيْرَ طَاقَتِي * وَمِنْ أَجْلِهِمْ قَامَتْ عَلَيَّ قِيَامَتِي
اَلاَفَارْ فَقُوا يَاهَا جِرُونَ بِمُهْجَتِي * فَقَدْرَقَّ لِي مِنْ بَعْدِكُمْ كُلُّ شَامِتِ
وَلَا تَبْخَلُوْا اَنْ تَسْمَحُوْا لِيْ بِنَظْرَةٍ * تُخَفِّفُ اَحْوِ اِلِيْ وَفَرْطَ صَبَابَتِيْ
سَانَتْ فُؤَادِى الصَّبْرُ عَنْكُمْ فَقَالَ لِي * اِلَيْكَ فَاِنَّ الصَّبْرَ مِنْ غَيْرِ عَادَتِي
sentences.tr:
hum ḥammalūnī fī al-hawā ghayra ṭāqatī * wa-min ajlihim qāmat ʿalayya qiyāmatī
alāfār faqū yāhā jirūna bi-muhjatī * fa-qad raqqa lī min baʿdikum kullu shāmiti
wa-lā tabkhalū an tasmaḥū lī bi-naẓratin * tukhaffifu aḥwi ilī wa-farṭa ṣabābatī
sānat fuʾādī al-ṣabru ʿankum fa-qāla lī * ilayka fa-inna al-ṣabra min ghayri ʿādatī
sentences.l:
They, they loaded me, in love, beyond my capacity * and on-account of them my resurrection has risen against me.
[Garbled; probably: Be gentle, O you who forsake,] with my heart's-blood * for after you every gloater has softened toward me.
And do not be stingy that you allow me a glance * that lightens [my states] and the excess of my longing.
Sānat my heart, the patience, away from you, and it said to me: * To-you! for patience is outside my habit.
sentences.i:
They burdened me in love beyond my strength, * and because of them my own day of reckoning has risen against me.
Be gentle, you who have left me, with my heart's blood, * for since you went even every gloater has pitied me.
Do not begrudge me the grant of one glance * to ease my state and the excess of my longing.
Away from you, patience [turned against] my heart and said to me, * "Away with you! Patience is not my way."
sentences.n: The print points these lines, and we copy them as printed. The second and third lines look corrupt, and we have kept every printed mark. In the second line the first words, اَلاَفَارْ فَقُوا يَاهَا جِرُونَ, are wrongly divided and pointed; the likeliest original is أَلَا ارْفُقُوا يَا هَاجِرُونَ, 'Be gentle, O you who forsake', and our best sense follows that. The rest of that line is sound, though its last word شَامِتِ is printed with a kasra and no tanwīn. In the third line تُخَفِّفُ اَحْوِ اِلِيْ is garbled: probably تُخَفِّفُ أَحْوَالِي, 'that lightens my states', and we read it so. In the fourth line سَانَتْ is obscure; it may be a slip for صَانَتْ, 'guarded', or for something meaning 'wronged' or 'grieved'. Our sense of that line is a guess, and we leave سَانَتْ untranslated in the literal layer. اِلَيْكَ is the interjection 'Away with you!'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ زَادَ فِي بُكَائِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ لَاتَبْكِ وَاحْمَدِ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى عَلَى السَّلَامَةِ وَالْعَافِيَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma zāda fī bukāʾihi fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu lā-tabki wa-aḥmadi allāha taʿālā ʿalā al-salāmati wa-al-ʿāfiyati
sentences.l: Then he increased in his weeping, and the stoker said to him: Do not weep, and praise God, exalted, for the safety and the well-being.
sentences.i: Then he wept the harder, and the stoker said to him: Do not weep, but thank God Most High for your safety and your health.
sentences.n: لَاتَبْكِ is printed as one word, lā-tabki, 'do not weep'. The second imperative وَاحْمَدِ takes a helping kasra before اللَّهَ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ كَمْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Ḍawʾu al-makāni kam baynanā wa-bayna Dimashqa
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: How much between us and between Damascus?
sentences.i: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: How far is it from here to Damascus?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ سِتَّةُ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sittatu ayyāmin
sentences.l: And he said: Six days.
sentences.i: He said: Six days.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تُرْسِلَنِي إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Ḍawʾu al-makāni hal laka an tursilanī ilayhā
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: Is there for you that you send me to it?
sentences.i: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: Would you be willing to send me there?
sentences.n: هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ is a polite request, 'is it in you to …?', and takes the subjunctive.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ يَاسَيِّدِى كَيْفَ أَدَعُكَ تَرُوحُ وَحْدَكَ وَأَنْتَ شَابٌّ صَغِيرٌ وَغَرِيبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu yāsayyidī kayfa adaʿuka tarūḥu waḥdaka wa-anta shābbun ṣaghīrun wa-gharībun
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: O my lord, how do I leave you, you go alone, and you a young-man, small, and a stranger?
sentences.i: The stoker said to him: My lord, how can I let you go alone, when you are a young man, and a stranger?
sentences.n: أَدَعُكَ تَرُوحُ, 'I leave you (that) you go', has no conjunction between the two verbs; this is ordinary in colloquial and Middle Arabic. The edition prints يَاسَيِّدِى as one word with a final ى, and we keep both.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ شِئْتَ السَّفَرَ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ فَأَنَا الَّذِي أَرُوحُ مَعَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-in shiʾta al-safara ilā Dimashqa fa-anā alladhī arūḥu maʿaka
sentences.l: So if you wish the travel to Damascus, then I am the one who goes with you.
sentences.i: If you wish to make the journey to Damascus, then I am the one who will go with you.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ سَمِعَتْ وَأَطَاعَتْنِي زَوْجَتِي مِنِّي وَسَافَرَتْ مَعِي أَقَمْتُ هُنَاكَ فَإِنَّهُ لَايَهُونُ عَلَيَّ فِرَاقُكَ
sentences.tr: wa-in samiʿat wa-aṭāʿatnī zawjatī minnī wa-sāfarat maʿī aqamtu hunāka fa-innahu lā-yahūnu ʿalayya firāquka
sentences.l: And if she heard and obeyed me, my wife, from me, and travelled with me, I stayed there, for it is not easy upon me, your parting.
sentences.i: And if my wife listens to me, obeys me, and travels with me, I will stay there with you, for I cannot bear to part from you.
sentences.n: This sentence is tangled in the print and the sense is partly guessed. The word order, with زَوْجَتِي مِنِّي placed after the two verbs, and the bare perfect أَقَمْتُ with no particle in the answer to the condition, are loose; we read it as 'if my wife agrees and comes along, I will settle there'. لَايَهُونُ is printed as one word. The edition prints a shadda on عَلَيَّ, and we keep it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ الْوَقَّادُ لِزَوْجَتِهِ هَلْ لَكِ أَنْ تُسَافِرِي مَعِي إِلَى دِمَشْقَ الشَّامِ أَوْتَكُونِي مُقِيمَةً هُنَا حَتَّى أُوصِلَ سَيِّدِي هَذَا إِلَى دِمَشْقَ الشَّامِ وَأَعُودَ إِلَيْكِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla al-waqqādu li-zawjatihi hal laki an tusāfirī maʿī ilā Dimashqa al-Shāmi awtakūnī muqīmatan hunā ḥattā uwṣila sayyidī hādhā ilā Dimashqa al-Shāmi wa-aʿūda ilayki
sentences.l: Then the stoker said to his wife: Is there for you that you travel with me to Damascus of-Syria, or you be staying here until I bring-to-arrival my lord this to Damascus of-Syria, and return to you?
sentences.i: Then the stoker said to his wife: Will you travel with me to Damascus in Syria, or will you stay here until I have brought this master of mine to Damascus and come back to you?
sentences.n: اوتكوني is printed as one word, أَوْ تَكُونِي, 'or you be'. 'Damascus of the Shām' is the city of Damascus in Syria, al-Shām being the whole Syrian region.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ يَطْلُبُ دِمَشْقَ الشَّامِ فَإِنِّي وَاللَّهِ لَايَهُونُ عَلَيَّ فِرَاقُهُ وَأَخَافُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ قُطَّاعِ الطَّرِيقِ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu yaṭlubu Dimashqa al-Shāmi fa-innī wa-allāhi lā-yahūnu ʿalayya firāquhu wa-akhāfu ʿalayhi min quṭṭāʿi al-ṭarīqi
sentences.l: For he seeks Damascus of-Syria, and I, by God, it is not easy upon me, his parting, and I fear for him from the cutters-of the road.
sentences.i: For he is bound for Damascus, and by God I cannot bear to part from him, and I fear for him on account of highwaymen.
sentences.n: قُطَّاعُ الطَّرِيقِ, 'the cutters of the road', is the usual phrase for highwaymen. The edition prints a shadda on عَلَيَّ, and we keep it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ زَوْجَتُهُ أُسَافِرُ مَعَكُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu zawjatuhu usāfiru maʿakumā
sentences.l: And his wife said to him: I travel with you both.
sentences.i: His wife said to him: I will travel with you both.
sentences.n: أُسَافِرُ with no particle can be read as a statement ('I will travel') or as a question ('shall I travel?'). The answer that follows shows she agrees, so we read it as a statement.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَقَّادُ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى الْمُوَافَقَةِ وَتَمَّ الْأَمْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-waqqādu al-ḥamdu li-allāhi ʿalā al-muwāfaqati wa-tamma al-amru
sentences.l: And the stoker said: The praise is to God for the agreement; and the matter was completed.
sentences.i: The stoker said: Praise be to God for this agreement. And so the matter was settled.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَقَّادَ قَامَ وَبَاعَ أَمْتِعَتَهُ وَأَمْتِعَةَ زَوْجَتِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-waqqāda qāma wa-bāʿa amtiʿatahu wa-amtiʿata zawjatihi
sentences.l: Then indeed the stoker rose and sold his goods and the goods of his wife.
sentences.i: Then the stoker got up and sold his belongings and his wife's.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الم—باح
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-m—bāḥ
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving off the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The archive prints the last word truncated and hyphenated, as الم—باح, with an em dash standing in for the missing letters and no vowel marks. We copy it exactly as printed. It is the usual الْمُبَاحِ, 'the permitted', of the closing formula, and the night ends there.
